clue.text: Notice name on the door

parts.note: a notice pinned up on a wall is a poster

explanation.surface: Someone's name is posted up as a notice on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side gate, a secondary entrance to a castle or building.

clue.text: Sportswear giving an advantage to oarsmen

parts.note: a plus is an advantage or asset
fours are rowing crews of four oarsmen

explanation.surface: Some kit gives rowers a competitive edge.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUS-FOURS are baggy knee-length trousers traditionally worn by golfers, cut four inches longer than ordinary knickerbockers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus-fours are loose breeches long associated with golf, so they are clothing for sport.

clue.text: Regulating the environment

definitions.meaning: adjusting a dial, clock or thermostat to the right level
the surroundings or backdrop in which something happens

explanation.surface: Controlling the climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting a thermostat is putting it to a level, and a story's backdrop or surroundings is also called this.

clue.text: Worried, being cut off without a sovereign

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for cut off goes around the monarch

parts.note: excised means cut off or removed, as by surgery
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the reigning sovereign

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious after being disinherited without even a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. The surface pushes 'sovereign' as a gold coin, but it is the monarch, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exercised about something is to be troubled or agitated by it.

clue.text: A rising French doctor is paralysed

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the piece is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the French for a is un, which the word French tells us
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A French doctor rises from the bed but cannot move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' asks for the French word for 'A' rather than the letter itself; 'rising' turns that word upward because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being numb means having no feeling or power of movement, like a limb that will not respond.

clue.text: In a letter, express one's preference for buff

indicators.note: In tells us the voting phrase sits inside the spelt-out letter

parts.note: DEE is the letter D written out as a word
to vote is to express one's preference at the ballot box

explanation.surface: In correspondence, someone states a liking for the colour buff.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast, someone devoted to a pastime, as in a film buff.

clue.text: Methodical composer's not second class

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for second is dropped from the composer's name

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer, best known for the ballet Coppélia
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A composer's work is anything but second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate actions are careful and unhurried, carried out in a planned, measured way.

clue.text: Say nothing evil about it

indicators.note: about means the word for evil goes around the zero

parts.note: vice is wickedness, evil
O, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet about wrongdoing: speak no evil.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to put it into words, to express it.

clue.text: Support expressed in various letters

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are set out in a varied order

explanation.surface: Encouragement expressed in a number of written messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs and crossbar that holds up a table top.

clue.text: Fifty men enough to hold back hostile force

indicators.note: back means the held run of letters is read in reverse
to hold means the letters sit within the words Fifty men enough

explanation.surface: Fifty soldiers should be enough to repel an attacking army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' gives the run YMENE inside 'Fifty men enough', and 'back' turns it round. Fifty is not L here.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an opposing army, the side fighting against you.

clue.text: 'ound that's free

parts.note: hound as a verb means hunt; the apostrophe drops the h, Cockney fashion, so the chasing word loses its h too
that's is that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A Cockney points out a dog that's off the leash.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ound marks a dropped H, so hound (to chase, hunt) becomes 'unt in the same accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a tethered thing is to undo its knot, releasing it.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly, quiet boy introduced to girl

indicators.note: introduced to means the quiet boy is put inside the girl's name

parts.note: Millie is a girl's name
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A shy lad is introduced to a girl, who thinks him a creep.
explanation.definitionFit: A millipede is a many-legged arthropod, the sort of bug people call a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Drawback, say, of a bird without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the bird goes around the money

parts.note: a finch is a small seed-eating songbird
L, from Latin libra, stands for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: The disadvantage of keeping a pet bird when you have no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' reads as a disadvantage, but 'say' tells you to hear it as 'draw back', a recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A flinch is a sudden recoil, an instance of drawing back in fear or pain.

clue.text: Moved in with skill, but without thought

indicators.note: in places the moved word inside the word for skilful manner

parts.note: ably means with skill
sent means moved, either dispatched or thrilled

explanation.surface: Someone moved house competently yet carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something absently is doing it inattentively, with the mind elsewhere.

clue.text: Made fine distinctions when rewriting parish list

indicators.note: rewriting suggests the words are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A pedant quibbled while the parish register was being revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is to argue over tiny, trivial differences.

clue.text: You prefer observing the rules in the closing moves

indicators.note: in the closing means take the closing letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A chess player prefers to stick to the rules in the endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the closing' asks for the last letters of 'You prefer observing the rules'. 'moves' looks like chess moves; it is the verb meaning impels.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to drive or impel them to act, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Pat can repent moving about

indicators.note: about means the shuffled word wraps around the can
moving suggests the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Pat is able to show remorse while bustling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name, but it is the adjective meaning apt. 'moving' rearranges the letters of repent into PERENT, and 'about' wraps that round the can.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat as an adjective means apt or neatly fitting, so a pat remark is relevant.

clue.text: On the whole, the classes are initially popular with the student

indicators.note: are initially says the classes are preceded at the start by the popular word

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
genera, plural of genus, are classes in biology
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Overall, the lessons were popular with the pupil from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classes' suggests school lessons, but here it means groups in biology. 'are initially' puts the popular word first, and the learner's letter comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or for the most part, as a broad rule.

clue.text: With respect he created a feeling of horror

indicators.note: created suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Out of politeness, a man produced a frightening atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The creeps is an informal phrase for a shuddering sense of fear or revulsion.

clue.text: Water drops fish by the bank

parts.note: to spin is to fish with a revolving lure, a spinner
a drift is a bank of snow or sand heaped up by the wind

explanation.surface: Water trickles off as an angler catches a fish beside the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is spray blown from the crests of waves, a fine shower of sea droplets.

clue.text: If I had my way, I would marry after the end of June

indicators.note: after places the marrying word behind the month's last letter

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I would

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of the month's name

parts.note: to ally is to join or unite, as in marriage

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a wedding just as June comes to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best possible case, as one would wish things to be.

clue.text: Jar that sounds impressive

indicators.note: sounds signals a word spoken like the word for impressive

parts.note: great means impressive or grand

explanation.surface: A pot whose name sounds rather grand.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate is to jar, to have an irritating, rasping effect on the nerves.

clue.text: Everyone, say, starts to run off at speed

parts.note: all means everyone
e.g., for example, is another way of writing say

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Everybody begins to sprint away quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo.

clue.text: Appropriate, your secret

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for yourself, to steal
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A fitting confidence for you to keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive, done covertly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: They help you to see and hear marks

indicators.note: hear signals the word for marks as spoken, not as written

parts.note: specks are tiny marks or spots

explanation.surface: Gadgets that help you see and hear the marks you were given.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs is short for spectacles, glasses worn to correct eyesight.

clue.text: Rope used to train horse to be a thruster

definitions.meaning: a long rein on which a trainer exercises a horse in circles
to make a sudden forward thrust, as a fencer does

explanation.surface: A lead rein needed to make a horse push forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the long training rein for exercising horses and the verb for a sudden forward jab.

clue.text: Sportsman left in a temper

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the word for temper

parts.note: anger is temper, rage

explanation.surface: An athlete walked out in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a fisherman, someone whose sport is fishing with rod and line.

clue.text: Roadside check, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for check is heard, not written

parts.note: to curb is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A traffic stop seems to be happening by the road.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling of the stone edging; American English spells both senses CURB.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb is the raised edge of a pavement beside the road.

clue.text: Inelegant wild flower

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy-looking bloom growing in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Scoundrel and libertine who captured Peggy's heart

indicators.note: who captured means the libertine encloses the letter at the heart of the girl's name

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the name

explanation.surface: A cad and rake stole Peggy's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled man, a rascal.

clue.text: Timidity gives one a head start at the beginning

indicators.note: at the beginning puts the start word in front of the headland

parts.note: to shy is to start or jump aside in fright, as a horse does
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone is given an advantage right at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head start' reads as one phrase meaning an advantage. Split it: the headland word with the startled-jump word placed at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyness is bashfulness, a reluctance to put oneself forward.

clue.text: Cry about love gone wrong — get swollen

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the crying word is read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry, weep noisily
love is nil in tennis scores, written as O
u/s, unserviceable, describes something broken or gone wrong

explanation.surface: Weeping over a failed romance leaves one puffy-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BLUB round to BULB. US is u/s, the British abbreviation for unserviceable, used of anything broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulbous means bulging and rounded, fat like a plant bulb.
